## Counting Multiples of 503

Since $462 < 503$ and $503$ is prime, the factorial $462!$ contains no factor of $503$; from $\binom{462}{r}\, r!\,(462-r)! = 462!$, it follows that $503 \nmid r!$ and $503 \nmid (462-r)!$ for $r \le 462$, so
$$503 \nmid \binom{462}{r} \quad \text{for } 0 \le r \le 462.$$
Thus $S_r$ is a multiple of $503$ **exactly when** $\binom{462}{r} = 0$, i.e., when
$$463 \le r \le 501 .$$
(In particular $S_0 \equiv \binom{462}{0} = 1 \pmod{503}$, so $S_0$ is not a multiple.)

The number of such indices is
$$501 - 463 + 1 = 502 - 463 = 39.$$
